findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "what_changed" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Call this when you have a handle from watch_free and you want what changed on that free watch. Free. Pass handle from watch_free (token is the same value). Read…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "what_changed" references sensitive artifacts (bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: preflight, check_mcp_setup, what_changed, find, seller_self_check · Private data: watch_free, what_changed, seller_self_check · Public sink: check_mcp_setup, watch_free, what_changed, seller_self_check · Destructive: seller_self_check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: preflight, check_mcp_setup, what_changed, find, seller_self_check · Private data: watch_free, what_changed, seller_self_check · Public sink: check_mcp_setup, watch_free, what_changed, seller_self_check · Destructive: seller_self_check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
